noKoreanVoice.title: No Korean voice on this device
noKoreanVoice.windows: Go to Windows Settings > Time & language > Speech > Add voices, install Korean, then reopen the browser. Microsoft Edge also offers natural Korean online voices (SunHi, InJoon).
noKoreanVoice.mac: Go to System Settings > Accessibility > Read & Speak > System voice > Manage voices, download a Korean voice (e.g. Yuna), then reopen the browser.
noKoreanVoice.ios: Go to Settings > Accessibility > Read & Speak > Voices > Korean, download a voice, then reopen Safari.
noKoreanVoice.android: Go to Settings > General management (or System) > Text-to-speech, set the engine to Google Speech Services and install Korean voice data.
noKoreanVoice.other: This browser has no Korean voice. Try Chrome or Edge.

recording.title: Can I save it as MP3?
recording.body: No. Browser speech synthesis plays straight to your speakers, so a web page cannot capture it as a file. That is why there is no download button. If you need a file, try one of these:
items: Windows: record the browser window with sound using Win+Alt+R (Xbox Game Bar)
macOS: built-in screen recording (Shift+⌘+5) does not capture system audio, so a separate audio capture tool is needed
Phones: enable internal/media sound in screen recording
For YouTube narration, use this tool to time your script, then record your own voice for the most natural result

usage.title: How to Use
items: Enter text and press the play button
Adjust voice, speed, and pitch as needed
Uses the browser's Web Speech API
Supports Korean, English, and many other languages

tips.title: Usage Tips
items: Study: listen at 'Slow (0.8x)' and shadow the audio to practice pronunciation.
Presentations: check the estimated duration to time your talk. People usually speak a little slower.
Narration drafts: if a sentence spans more than two lines in the reader, consider splitting it.
On Windows, Microsoft Edge's online (Natural) voices sound the most natural; in Chrome, the Google voices are a good choice.

whatIs.title: What is Text-to-Speech (TTS)?
whatIs.description: Text to Speech reads text aloud with your browser's built-in speech engine (Web Speech API). Long text is split into sentences so it plays without cut-offs, and the current sentence and word are highlighted. Your text is never sent to Toolhub's servers and no sign-up is needed. Voices marked 'Online', however, are synthesized on the voice provider's servers (Google, Microsoft, etc.), so the browser sends your text there.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Type or paste text. For text copied from a PDF with broken lines, use 'Clean line breaks/spaces'.
2. Choose a voice. Korean voices are listed first, and your voice and speed are remembered.
3. Press play to highlight each sentence and word (word highlighting depends on the voice and may not work with some). Click any sentence to start from there.
4. Space plays/pauses and Esc stops. Drag the progress bar to jump to a sentence.
5. Use 'Copy text link' to share the same text and speed.
6. Enable Repeat a passage, choose the first and last sentences and a repeat count. Use the pauses to read aloud.
7. Name and save a reading-list entry. Opening it replaces the current text and settings without starting playback. Deleting an entry does not clear the open manuscript.

items.q: Can it read long text continuously?
items.a: Text is split by sentence and length for sequential playback. Support and interruptions depend on the device, browser and voice. If playback fails, you can inspect the failed sentence and explicitly retry it.

items.q: Can I save it as an MP 3?
items.a: Browser speech synthesis plays straight to the speakers, so a web page cannot save it as a file. Use screen recording with sound (Win+Alt+R on Windows, phone screen recording) if you need one.

items.q: There is no Korean voice in the list.
items.a: Voices come from your OS and browser. When no Korean voice exists, the tool shows device-specific install steps. On Windows, add Korean under Settings > Time & language > Speech.
Voices installed on your device work offline. Voices marked 'online' need an internet connection.

items.q: Can I save a manuscript and its reading position?
items.a: Select Save to reading list to keep up to eight entries in this browser. Names allow 40 characters and text allows 30,000 characters (some emoji count as two); oversized text is not silently truncated. Open an entry to replace the current text, settings and position, then start playback yourself. Playback and repeat rounds do not resume automatically.

items.q: Will the same voice and position work on another device?
items.a: The list is local to this browser and does not sync through an account. If a saved voice is unavailable or sentence boundaries differ, review the notice and choose a voice or starting position. A device-only voice preference is not silently replaced with a remote voice.
